extracted.intended_audience: administrative law practitioners, federal agency officials, policymakers, and researchers interested in ACUS processes
extracted.subtask_description: Description of the Administrative Conference of the United States (ACUS) process for producing Recommendations and occasional Statements about administrative and regulatory processes, including roles, approvals, and implementation responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory function: convene public and private sectors to recommend improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: The main statutory function of ACUS is to bring together the public and private sectors to recommend improvements to administrative and regulatory processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is ACUS's central mission and frames all subsequent procedural steps; recommendations should aim to improve administrative/regulatory processes via collaboration between public and private participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to engage consultants (Office of the Chairman + Council approval)
rubrics_metrics.description: ACUS’s Office of the Chairman, with the approval of the Council, engages consultants to study administrative processes or procedures that may need improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement of outside consultants requires Office of the Chairman action and Council approval; this establishes who commissions studies and the need for internal oversight before studies begin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive research report proposing recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultants or in-house staff then prepare a comprehensive research report proposing recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports are expected to be comprehensive and to propose specific recommendations; this step creates the substantive basis for committee discussion and drafting. Emphasis on thoroughness and actionable proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee discussion and draft Recommendation preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: An ACUS committee discusses this report, preparing a draft Recommendation to submit to the Council and, with approval, to the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A committee-level deliberation transforms the research report into a draft Recommendation; the draft is then routed to the Council for approval before going to the Assembly. Committee work is the primary forum for refining proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council/Assembly approval, debate, adoption, and ACUS implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Following a debate the Assembly adopts the final Recommendation, which ACUS undertakes to implement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final adoption requires Assembly debate and vote following Council approval; once adopted, ACUS is responsible for undertaking implementation of the Recommendation. This defines the approval chain and the institution's commitment to act on adopted recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Statements as an alternative to formal Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: On occasion, the ACUS membership has acted to adopt a “Statement” to express its views on a particular matter without making a formal recommendation on the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements are typically produced by the same process that leads to Recommendations but may set forth issues, conclusions from a study, or comments rather than recommendations. ACUS has adopted 20 such statements, which are included in the searchable database of recommendations.
